h: Owls in the Morning, Sea Air by Lunchtime
p: Kirkleatham is a little gem of a village, and the owl centre is part of a wider cluster of things to see. Kirkleatham Museum, set in a handsome old hall, covers the history of the local area, from the seaside to the steelworks, so you can easily turn a quick owl visit into a fuller morning. The village also has the impressive old almshouses known as Sir William Turner's Hospital, a reminder of how long people have been living and building here. The grounds around the museum are lovely for a stroll on a dry day.

At the owl centre itself, take it slowly. Many owls sit perfectly still, blending into their perches, and part of the fun for children is spotting them before the grown-ups do. Read the signs as you go, as there are great titbits about how owls hunt, why they can turn their heads so far and how their feathers let them fly almost silently. It's ideal for curious kids who like a fact or two.

Back on the coast, Redcar's beach is a long stretch of sand looking out at the offshore wind farm, and film buffs might like to know the seafront was used for the Dunkirk scenes in the 2007 film Atonement. A few miles along the coast, Saltburn-by-the-Sea has a Victorian pier and a cliff lift that carries you between the town and the sands, plus a seafront that's a favourite with surfers. Teesside also offers plenty of country walks, so you've got options whatever the weather is up to.
